pageCache.pageTitle: British Values –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
British Values
The British Values play a very important role in our school.We explore what it means to be British by writing speeches about the values. We then presented some of the best ones to our Mayor. We have also had many assemblies in which we discussed our British Values. All this learning about Great Britain and what it means to be British culminated in our British Values Day. During this amazing day, every class in our school used their art, writing and debating skills to produce excellent work which we displayed all around the school. British Values have helped us to consider who we are and it has helped us to define what makes our country such a special one.
According to Ofsted, ‘fundamental British values’ are:
At St Saviour’s we uphold these core values and along with our own set of Values aim to instill these in our children, teachers and the wider community. We are all very proud to be British.

pageCache.pageTitle: Headteacher’s Welcome –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Headteacher’s Welcome
Welcome to St. Saviour’s Church of England Primary School.
We are a 2-form entry school based in the heart of Walthamstow; a culturally rich and diverse borough which was once home to celebrated achievers such as William Morris and Harry Kane.
We are one of three schools who form Genesis Education Trust – one of the highest achieving academy trusts in England. We collaborate, share, celebrate and work well together with the other schools in the trust but firmly retain our own individuality to serve our local communities.
‘Let God transform you into a new person by changing the way that you think.’ – Romans 12:2 – Our school vision is rooted in the Christian narrative from Romans 12. Children are encouraged to break away from conforming and to look at the world through God’s eyes; using their gifts to transform themselves, others and the community. Our vision is for the common good of the whole community and drives our commitment in ensuring that all children flourish as set out in the Church of England document, ‘Valuing All God’s Children’.
Through transformation away from conformed thinking, we teach our children to become well-rounded and aspirational, leading them to live a successful life and becoming universal leaders through the teaching of global competencies. We recognise that little voices can have a big impact and our Young Transformers Programme offers children regular opportunities to develop personally and apply learned skills through acts of advocacy. We are proud of our children’s efforts and their responsibility towards wider issues and this is something that we strongly encourage.
Our school values: Faith, Forgiveness, Respect, Truth, Love, Tenacity and Serenity underpin our school vision and the ethos of the school. They include every interaction in school life and are lived by the whole school community. We hope that our children grow to become ethical individuals directed by our Christian values which results in them being moral-led ambitious learners. Our vision means that by the time our children leave at eleven, they will be confident, independent learners, with enquiring minds, have a lifelong love of learning and a thoughtful and considerate approach to life.
At St Saviour’s we have incredible children, amazing teachers, fantastic resources, a beautiful building and we live amongst a wonderful community which we strive to serve. Our school site is blessed with beautiful grounds and a Forest School. Each year group enjoys sessions with a trained Forest School leader where the children develop a range of skills, build confidence and self esteem and have lots of fun immersing themselves in the outdoors!
We believe passionately in the importance of strong relationships between home and school and take every opportunity to work in partnership with our families. Together we can provide the best possible support for our students to become lifelong learners, responsible citizens and resilient and successful people. In our globally diverse and competitive world, we are passionate about ensuring that ,alongside an outstanding curriculum, our children are provided with unique experiences and opportunities for enrichment to ensure that they reach their full potentials.
Thank you for showing an interest in our wonderful school and please do not hesitate to contact us if you require any further information or would like a visit.
Mr Lemouchi Headteacher

Welcome to St Saviour’s School.
Welcome to St. Saviour’s Church of England Primary School and thank you for taking an interest in our wonderful school.
We are a 2-form entry school based in the heart of Walthamstow, a culturally rich and diverse borough which was once home to celebrated achievers such as Harry Kane and William Morris.
Our school forms a part of an academy trust, Genesis Education Trust, that is one of the highest achieving academy trusts in England. We collaborate, share, celebrate and work well together with the other schools in the trust but firmly retain our own individuality to serve our local communities.
The school vision: Let God transform you into a new person by changing the way that you think – Romans 12:2 NLT
Through transformation away from conformed thinking, we teach our children to become well-rounded and aspirational, leading them to live a successful life and becoming universal leaders through the teaching of global competencies.
We hope that our children grow to become ethical individuals directed by our Christian values which results in them being moral-led ambitious learners. Our vision means that by the time our children leave at eleven, they will be confident, independent learners, with enquiring minds, have a lifelong love of learning and a thoughtful and considerate approach to life.
At St Saviour’s we have great children, amazing teachers, fantastic resources, a beautiful building and we live amongst a wonderful community. We want to help everyone learn. We will always try our best to serve our local community.
As headteacher, I am passionate about providing our children an array of enrichment opportunities and expose them to unique opportunities. Some of these include horse-riding, kayaking, archery, fencing and much more. We are also working hard to establish global links to enable all of our children to become global citizens with strong knowledge and understanding of the world.
We work hard to give your children the best opportunities which means that as a trust, we invest in our staff with continued professional development. We believe that we are all life-long learners and want to ensure that our staff are fully equipped in providing your children the best opportunities. The school site is blessed with beautiful grounds which house our three alpacas. The Year 6 children also have their own dedicated building which helps prepare them for life in secondary school.
As a church school, we have always sought to express our Christian ethos in practical ways that make a difference. This has included a wide range of courageous advocacy from our children where they have actively supported causes including climate change, sustainability, poverty and homelessness. We are proud of our children’s efforts and their responsibility towards wider issues and this is something that we strongly encourage.
Faith, Forgiveness, Respect, Truth, Love, Tenacity and Serenity
are associated with our school vision and underpin the ethos of the school. They are intended to include every interaction in school life and are lived by the whole school community.
Thank you for showing an interest in the school and please do not hesitate to contact the school if you require any further information or would like a visit.
Amir Lemouchi Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: About the Governors –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
About the Governors
St Saviour’s has an excellent Governing Body from a diverse background and each member brings a unique set of skills to our school. Anyone aged 18 or over can become a school governor. No specialist qualifications are needed and people from many different backgrounds volunteer for the role. Enthusiasm, commitment and an interest in education are the most important qualities.
You don’t need to have a family member attending a school or college to become a governor. As a school or college governor, your duties will include: assessing the strategic direction, policies and objectives approving the budget reviewing progress against the budget and objectives challenging and supporting senior staff playing a part in appointing staff.
The governing body in schools and colleges is made up of: staff representatives community governors, including parents or students other local sponsors, like businesses Governing bodies make their decisions based on the advice of committees. Governing bodies in schools and colleges are accountable for: the use of public funds the quality of education provided the wider contribution to the community.

By email: st-saviours-school@genesistrust.net

pageCache.pageTitle: Project Vision –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Project Vision
At Genesis Education Trust, we pride ourselves on the continuous progress,attainment and achievements of our pupils across all the curriculum subjects. For our pupils to be confident, independent learners with enquiring minds and a life-long love of learning, we offer outstanding teaching and learning provision alongside broad, experiential and memorable activities. Our Young Transformers programme offers just that. The programme is intrinsically linked to our biblical vision:
‘Romans 12:2: Let God transform you into a new person by changing the way you think.‘
We firmly believe that young people do not only have the power to transform themselves into responsible and proactive citizens but also the community they serve. In fact, our mission to transform the world for the goodness of all its citizens is so strong that we offer every child in our three schools the opportunity to actively participate in amazing transformative experiences throughout their time at school. We want our children to have the knowledge and power to shape the world they live in.
Young Transformers sets out to challenge children across five branches:Creative, Community, Curious, Caring and Confidence
Creative – In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth
Community -But if we walk in the light, as he is in the light, we have fellowship with one another
Curious – It is the glory of God to conceal things, but the glory of kings is to search things out
Caring -Let each of you look not only to his own interests, but also to the interests of others.
Confidence – I can do all things through him who strengthens me.
Throughout their time in primary school, each child will engage with aspirational activities in and out of school with the power to transform on a larger or smaller scale. This could mean from learning how to make your bed at home to making fresh food parcels for families in our community.
As always, we work closely with our local church and Chelmsford’s Diocese on projects they support to further enable our pupils to make a change for the greater good. Together, we set out an approach to life that reflects core biblical values and principles and is rooted in the belief that God loves each of us equally.

pageCache.pageTitle: Our Christian Vision –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Our Christian Vision
Our School Ethos
The ethos of St. Saviour’s C of E Primary School is to work together to extend Jesus’ model of the Kingdom of God on earth by living out a lifestyle through the Christian values and according to his teaching. We are inspired by his message, life and example through which God’s unconditional love for all people is expressed.
Whilst we serve a richly diverse community of children from a wide range of faiths and backgrounds, we seek to preserve and develop the religious character of our school in accordance with the principles of the Church of England and in partnership with the Churches at parish and diocesan level. This enables our children to be reflective and morally ground by associating their daily actions to our school values.
Our School Vision
Let God transform you into a new person by changing the way that you think.’
Romans 12:2
Our vision is for St Saviour’s to be a place of transforming growth, where Christian education inspires children and adults for achievement in the whole of life. Our vision reflects spirituality, beliefs about ourselves and each other and beliefs about the world.
Spirituality Our vision will ensure that we provide opportunities for pupils to develop independence and confidence within their beliefs whilst providing space for enquiry and reflection into their understanding of God and the principles by which they live. Opportunities for prayer, quiet reflection and open discussion and dialogue are integral to our approach. We want to ensure pupils have a lifelong desire for spiritual development.
Beliefs about ourselves and each other We believe that every adult and child is precious no matter what race, sex, religion, social background, physical or intellectual ability. We recognise the uniqueness of each child and ensure that they develop the skills they need to flourish academically, physically, mentally and spiritually regardless of their background or individual needs.
Beliefs about the world The ethos of St. Saviour’s School is to work together to extend Jesus’ model of the Kingdom of God on Earth by living out a lifestyle through the Christian values and according to his teaching. We are inspired by his message, life and example through which God’s unconditional love for all people is expressed. Children are challenged to transform their thinking, enquire, ask questions and reflect upon the world in which they live in order to develop their understanding. Through understanding comes responsibility and we ensure children learn through our curriculum and times of worship their responsibility to the environment, helping others and living well with one another.
Living out our Vision We strive to show Love, Truth, Respect, Forgiveness, Tenacity, Serenity and have Faith. We show this in our behaviour, our work and our relationships. Our curriculum encourages enquiry as children discover for themselves and encourages self-evaluation and reflection.. We encourage the whole development of each and every child as a person made in God’s image; unique, special and deeply loved by their maker. As a church school, we have always sought to express our Christian ethos in practical ways that make a difference and our Young Transformers programme offers children opportunities to transform themselves and others by taking action.
Our School Values
We believe that every adult and child is precious no matter what race, sex, religion, social background, physical or intellectual ability.
Our school values: Faith, Forgiveness, Respect, Truth, Love, Tenacity and Serenity underpin our school vision and the ethos of the school. They include every interaction in school life and are lived by the whole school community. We hope that our children grow to become ethical individuals directed by our Christian values which results in them being moral-led ambitious learners.

pageCache.pageTitle: Worship Council –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Worship Council
Worship Councillors 2025-2026
The Worship Council are a very important part of school life at St Saviour’s.
They help to lead Collective Worship every day; taking responsibility to put the reflections slides and the entry music on whilst all the classes come into the hall and to lead prayers and worship. They choose songs for the collective worship using pupil voice and they monitor the worship and prayer areas around the school and in the classrooms to make sure they reflect how important worship is to us at St Saviour’s.
Pupil voice is important and they conduct pupil voice questionnaires to our classes and report back to the rest of the Worship Council during meetings.We have regular meetings to discuss how worship is going at our school and ways we can further improve worship and reflection at St Saviour’s.

pageCache.pageTitle: Curriculum –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum
Our curriculum ensures excellent coverage of the National Curriculum (Years 1-6) and Foundation Stage Early Years Curriculum (Reception Children). We have fully embraced the higher expectations set out in both curriculums and have devised our own units of work for each subject area so that we can ensure a sound progression of learning. We also have a core team of specialist teachers who are passionate about their curriculum area; these teachers work with different groups of children each year. Our team includes PE, music, art and computing specialists.
Our Reception pupils learn both indoors and outdoors, experiencing a range of adult led and child initiated activities. We value and incorporate the children’s interests as they develop. As children approach their final half term of reception, they start to prepare for their transition to year 1 and begin to experience key stage 1 learning. In years 1-6, we ensure that this ‘active’ and ‘engaging’ learning continues, with teachers maximising opportunities for talk time, active, visual, audio learning and the use of the outdoors. At all times, we focus on learning being challenging, engaging and enjoyable.
At St Saviour’s we believe that children learns best when they are excited about their learning; for this reason, we teach a themed approach where possible. Through making strong links across curriculum areas, children begin to make connections and the learning experience is much richer. Children in year 1-6 also take part in a project exhibition, where they get to showcase their project work that was completed over the termly holiday –this is always a great celebration.
In addition to everyday teaching, we have a range of learning opportunities that further enhance the curriculum. We arrange workshops both within and outside of school so that children get to learn in different ways. Workshops children have enjoyed include a chocolate workshop for a unit of work about the Mayans and a great fire of London workshop. Children also visit a range of museums, galleries and centres of learning where they will often take part in workshops led by the staff at the venue e.g. the Natural History Museum, Imperial War Museum and Suntrap to name but a few.
The learning experience we provide is completed with the knowledge that each child is unique and special. As a Church of England Primary School, we place our Christian values at the heart of everything that we do; we live our values. Assemblies take place each week where children learn from the stories in the Bible. Each week, we focus one of our Christian Values. We also attend Church each half term. Each day we aim to fulfil our mission statement: ‘Educating for Life’ by encouraging the whole development of each and every child as a person made in God’s image and deeply loved by their Maker.
If you would like further information on our school curriculum please contact Mr Julie Toliday, Deputy Headteacher through the School Office.

pageCache.pageTitle: Forest School –  St Saviour's Church of England Primary School
pageCache.text:
Forest School
Each year group enjoys sessions with a trained Forest School Leader where the children develop a range of skills, build confidence and self esteem and have lots of fun immersing themselves in the outdoors!
Originating in Scandinavia, Forest School is a way of learning in a woodland environment. It offers children a chance to learn about, experience and gain respect for the natural world, whilst developing a range of skills in all areas of learning, in particular those associated with personal, social and emotional development. Children will have the opportunity to take part in den building, hunting for mini beasts, making mud pies and lots of craft activities using natural resources.
